- Expected tokens/month: approximately 120–180M tokens during the 90-day pilot.

2) Target cost per 1M tokens you’re budgeting for the pilot (you mentioned a target range—can you confirm a number you’d like us to aim for)?

I’ll loop in Rafael and Dev to propose a path that balances latency SLOs and unit cost (multi-path routing + batching + reserved capacity where it makes sense). I plan to send a draft estimate and next-steps doc tomorrow.

1) Estimated split: ~60% interactive (chat streaming) and ~40% background batch summarization. Interactive traffic tends to spike during business hours.
2) Budget target: we’re aiming for ~ $30 / 1M tokens for the pilot if possible. Overall monthly budget for the pilot is in the $3.5k–$6k range depending on how the latency/quality trade-offs land.

- For interactive sessions, p95 <= 300ms is required for acceptance testing; our product team will push for 150ms if costs are reasonable.

Folks — forwarding Lumidocs’ confirmation. Key asks:
- Volume: 120–180M tokens/mo (pilot)
- Split: ~60% streaming (interactive) / 40% batch (async summarization)
- Target: ~ $30 / 1M tokens (pilot target)
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms required; 150ms preferred for premium.
- Procurement: SOC2 evidence needed.

Proposed high-level approach (my draft):
1) Two-path routing: 
   - Path A (interactive/critical): Streaming-enabled model variant, reserved capacity to hit p95 <= 150–300ms depending on load; priced at premium unit rate.
   - Path B (background): Batched execution for summarization jobs with larger batch windows to maximize throughput and lower unit cost.
2) Autoscale + headroom policy: Configure burst capacity for short spikes to avoid request rejects (important to them).
3) Fall-back policy: Route to a slightly cheaper quantized variant or longer-latency batched path during extreme overloads.

Questions for engineering/pricing (Rafael / Dev):
- Rough unit cost delta: streaming per-1M vs batched per-1M at 120–180M scale (ballpark is fine).
- Trade-offs in reserved capacity sizing to guarantee 150ms p95 for their peak concurrency (~120 users).
- Any quick SOC2 evidence pack we can point procurement to.

I’ll draft an estimate workbook and routing diagram (attaching) — can you review and we’ll finalize a customer-facing estimate?

Thanks — Chloe

Subject: Lumidocs pilot — draft estimate & next steps

Hi Sarah / Ravi — thanks for confirming the split and the budget target. Attached is a short estimate workbook that shows two paths and a blended cost example. High level: 

- Estimated blended baseline (120M tokens / mo, 60/40 split) at proposed routing:
  • Path A (streaming, reserved capacity): unit estimate $42–$48 / 1M tokens — gives us headroom to hit p95 ~150–250ms in most windows with a small reserved pool.
  • Path B (batched, opportunistic batching): unit estimate $18–$24 / 1M tokens — for async summarization jobs where 500–1000ms latency is fine.
  • Blended unit: ~$32–$36 / 1M tokens depending on how much volume we can push into Path B. At 120M tokens, that implies ~$3.8k–$4.3k/month.

Observations & trade-offs:
- Hitting 150ms p95 consistently requires reserved capacity and results in higher unit cost because streaming reduces batching efficiency.
- If Lumidocs can shift more of the summarization volume into larger batch windows (increase Path B share to ~50%), blended unit cost drops toward their $30 / 1M target.
- Autoscale/bursting for short spikes avoids rejects but adds an overage component to the bill; we recommend a small burst pool to balance UX and budget.

Recommended next steps:
1) Confirm pilot duration (we suggest 90 days) and final target tokens/month for the pilot (pick a conservative number in the 120–180M range).
2) Approve two-path approach and pilot SLA (p95 acceptance threshold for interactive).
3) Redwood to provide: a) short SOC2 evidence pack; b) pricing worksheet (attached); c) kickoff date options.

If you’re comfortable with the approach I’ll turn this into a short one-page pilot agreement and send it over for signatures. Happy to jump on a call tomorrow to walk the workbook.

Thanks — Chloe
